sentence: This project builds a method that uses inexpensive microscopes to image blood vessels in post-mortem brains and how they interact with cancer cells.
This project studies how losing two genes in excitatory neurons changes the fate, position and survival of cortical interneurons in the mouse.
This project measures how stable protein structures are and how they change shape, for millions of proteins at once, to build predictive AI models.
This project uses rhesus macaques infected with a virus related to HIV to test whether engineered immune cells and stem cells can cure HIV.
This project uses several research approaches to study posttraumatic stress disorder, suicidal thoughts and behaviors, and substance misuse in Veterans.
This project builds a collection of kidney images to study cyst formation, growth and rupture in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
This project studies the molecular basis of how chemosensory systems adapt to help an organism exploit its environment.
This project provides mass spectrometry services that measure proteins and metabolites for basic science and clinical research studies.
This project uses synthetic DNA techniques to test how mutations in one gene and loss of other genes change blood levels of a clotting protein.
This project builds a machine learning system that maps how several genes interact with each other in cancer.
This project builds an antibody-drug conjugate to kill triple-negative breast cancer cells and activate immune cells in the tumor.
This project studies how vascular stem cells lose their stem cell traits and make matrix that causes fibrosis, using cultured cells and mouse models.
This project studies how epithelial and stromal cells work together to regenerate the intestinal epithelium after injury.
This project tests whether lowering the activity of a gene protects cartilage and joint tissue from osteoarthritis, inflammation and pain.
This project tries to rejuvenate mesenchymal stem cells to help skeletal muscle regenerate in diabetes and peripheral arterial disease.
This project tests a drug delivery system made of nanofibers that targets and stays in the lungs, combined with radiation therapy, to treat lung tumors.
This project tests whether targeting a repeat expansion mutation treats several spinocerebellar ataxias, and whether changes in alternative splicing can show it.
This project studies how tumor metabolism and immune cells interact in different types of bladder cancer, and tests inhibitors.
This project studies how a phosphatase and a kinase control the actin network that macrophages use for macropinocytosis, or cell drinking.
